details:
=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:32159-32195 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna]
  PROBLEM: On every rc 77 exit, the wave judge calls `_persist_orch_wave_check_unjudge judge_isolation_unavailable` (line 32188) without a guard, including when `wave_isolation_skipped=true` because the isolation latch is escalated (`ai:needs-human`) or labels are unavailable and no judge ran; this drops the `wave_check_judged` / `wave_check_judged_at` marker, while the `tg_notify` line just above is already gated on `wave_isolation_skipped`.
  WHY: With PERSIST_ORCH_WAVE_CHECK_ENABLED=true and a red integration PR, the `judged_hold` bound never applies, so every poll tick re-runs the full red path (check-runs read, Actions job-log read, `wave-check-block`, `attempt_journal.py append` wave_check/fail PATCH, state writes, `post_state_comment`) for as long as the latch is set. The `judge_failed` unjudge at line 32195 has the same effect when `max_attempts=0` (`JUDGE_PROMPT_CHARS > 1048576`), as flagged by anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 and minimax_minimax-m3. All reviewers rated it MAJOR.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:32066-32070 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: When the `gh_retry` check-runs request fails, the code truncates `${pwc_runs}` to an empty file, so `classify_check_runs` reports `outcome=unavailable` and `_persist_orch_wave_check_clear checks_unavailable` clears all state.
  WHY: The clear drops `wave_check_wait_since`, so a transient network failure restarts the boundary-first-seen hold on the next tick. The behaviour is fail-open, but it resets the wait clock.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
- requirement: P9 says, “Any failure” sets `INVOKE_JUDGE_FOR_STUCK=true` and runs the existing judge path.
  expected_change_site: `scripts/persist_orchestrator.py`, `classify_check_runs`, and its caller in `scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh`
  confidence=5
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, openai_gpt-6-luna]
  EVIDENCE: `classify_check_runs` only adds failed runs whose names are in `--required-names` (scripts/persist_orchestrator.py, lines 763-766), and the poller passes `ORCH_FINAL_MERGE_REQUIRED_CHECKS` (orchestrate_poll_process.sh, line 20187 / lines 20185-20189), so failed non-required checks (e.g. `copilot-pull-request-reviewer`) are classified green and the clean-wave skip can proceed. google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite notes this was disclosed and accepted in pass 1.
- requirement: “API: at most 2 calls per wave boundary per tick.”
  expected_change_site: `scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh`, `persist_orch_wave_check`
  confidence=5
  flagged_by: [openai_gpt-6-luna]
  EVIDENCE: The check-runs read occurs at line 20184. On a red result with an empty login cache, lines 20254-20256 make an identity read before the job-log read at line 20264, totaling three API reads. The cache is initialized empty at line 19494, and earlier population is conditional.
- requirement: P9 requires “one log tail of at most 8 KiB from the first failing check.”
  expected_change_site: `scripts/persist_orchestrator.py`, `classify_check_runs` and `render_wave_check_block`, with the log fetch in `scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh`
  confidence=4
  flagged_by: [openai_gpt-6-luna]
  EVIDENCE: Lines 773-782 select an Actions job log and a non-Actions summary independently. If a non-Actions check fails before an Actions check, the poller fetches the later Actions check’s log at `scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:20258-20264`; `render_wave_check_block` prefers that log over the earlier failure’s summary at `scripts/persist_orchestrator.py:898-904`.
- requirement: “Pair workflow/script changes with the contract tests the plan calls for.”
  expected_change_site: tests/test_orchestrate_poll_workflow_contract.py
  confidence=4
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  EVIDENCE: No contract test in `tests/test_orchestrate_poll_workflow_contract.py` verifies the `PERSIST_ORCH_WAVE_CHECK_ENABLED` flag persistence across the orchestrator polling workflow, only the environment defaults are verified.
=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:lines 32185-32190, the rc 77 exit of the wave judge: `[ "${wave_isolation_skipped:-false}" = true ] || tg_notify ...` and then `_persist_orch_wave_check_unjudge judge_isolation_unavailable` with no guard. The skipped case is set at lines 32159-32161; the unjudge helper is at lines 20032-20047. | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The unjudge helper is called on every rc 77 exit, including when `_judge_isolation_should_run` (lines 546-575) returned 1 because of an escalated latch with `ai:needs-human` or `labels_unavailable`, so no judge was attempted. The `tg_notify` on line 32187 is gated on `wave_isolation_skipped`, but the unjudge call on the next line is not, so the `wave_check_judged` / `wave_check_judged_at` marker is removed on the same tick.
  WHY: The `judged_hold` bound never applies. Every tick re-runs the check-runs read, the Actions job-log read, `wave-check-block`, a state write and `post_state_comment`, an `attempt_journal.py append` (PATCH, attempt_journal.py line 636) that adds a new wave_check/fail entry, and the unjudge state write with a second `post_state_comment`. Before this run the same scenario was one read per tick with no writes (`reason=judged_recently`). The same effect occurs on the `judge_failed` exit: when `JUDGE_PROMPT_CHARS > 1048576`, line 32132 sets `max_attempts=0` and the unjudge call on line 32195 drops the marker. Suggested fix: `[ "${wave_isolation_skipped:-false}" = true ] || _persist_orch_wave_check_unjudge judge_isolation_unavailable`, which keeps the existing test passing; optionally skip the call on line 32195 when `max_attempts` is 0.
- TASK COMPLETENESS: NONE. The P9 deliverables are present. Three items were not re-raised because earlier rounds accepted them: only required checks count as failures; the cached identity read can be a third read on a red tick; `log_job_id` uses the check-run id. Removing `# noqa: PLC0415` at tests/test_workflow_untrusted_input_contract.py line 986 has no effect, because pyproject.toml has no ruff configuration and CI runs `ruff check --select E,F` on scripts/*.py only (.github/workflows/ci.yml line 377).
- HARDENING_SUGGESTIONS (3 related items; HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 3):
  - scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh line 32188: guard the unjudge call with `wave_isolation_skipped` (1 line).
  - scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh line 32195: `[ "${max_attempts:-0}" -gt 0 ] && _persist_orch_wave_check_unjudge judge_failed`, checking that the test's "followed by continue" assertion still matches (1-2 lines).
  - tests/test_orchestrate_poll_process.py `test_persist_orch_wave_check_judge_no_verdict_drops_the_judged_marker`: add an assertion for the rc 77 isolation-skipped guard (2 lines).
=== END FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===

  PROBLEM: The `_persist_orch_wave_check_unjudge` helper removes `wave_check_judged` and `wave_check_judged_at` even when the judge run is skipped because isolation is escalated (`wave_isolation_skipped=true`).
  WHY: No judge runs but the marker is dropped. If the PR check stays red, every tick repeats the expensive path (check-runs read, job-log read, tracking comment update, state write) instead of holding.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:32066-32070 (gh_retry check) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: When `gh_retry` fails, `: > "${pwc_runs}"` produces an empty `check_runs.json`.
  WHY: `_check_run_pages` returns `None`, so the outcome is `unavailable` and `_persist_orch_wave_check_clear checks_unavailable` clears state, losing `wave_check_wait_since` and restarting the wait clock on transient network failures.

  Requirement: "Any failure" sets `INVOKE_JUDGE_FOR_STUCK=true`.
  Expected change site: `scripts/persist_orchestrator.py`, `classify_check_runs`, and its caller in `scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh`.

Failed non-required checks are classified green. (Disclosed/accepted in pass 1).

  Expected change site: tests/test_orchestrate_poll_workflow_contract.py.
  Evidence of absence: No contract test verifies `PERSIST_ORCH_WAVE_CHECK_ENABLED` flag persistence across the orchestrator polling workflow; only the environment defaults are verified.

  PROBLEM: The new unjudge call fires unconditionally on rc=77, including when `wave_isolation_skipped=true`, even though the sibling `tg_notify` line just above is already gated on `wave_isolation_skipped != true`.
  WHY: With a red PR, the flag enabled and the `ai:needs-human` latch set, the dropped marker makes every tick re-run the full red path: check-runs read, job-log read, an identity read if the cache is empty, `wave-check-block`, a wave_check/fail journal comment, state writes and `post_state_comment`. The same regression is reachable on the `judge_failed` branch at line 32195 when `max_attempts=0` (`JUDGE_PROMPT_CHARS > 1048576`).
